name: status
description: Whether Basalt is ready for you, and what to do if not. Call it at the start of a session before any other Basalt tool, after the person says they fixed something (started the engine, ran an upgrade, registered a passkey), and after a failure that looks like setup rather than your statement (UNAVAILABLE, GUARD_OUTDATED, SETUP_PENDING). Answers even when the engine is down. Each problem carries nextSteps: do them in order, show the person personMessage verbatim and every PERSON step's command unchanged. When operatedBy is PERSON you never start, stop or upgrade anything yourself; when it is AGENT you run the machine steps addressed to you (AGENT RUN_COMMAND). In either case never ask the person for, or accept, their database admin connection string or password. Read-only; never returns a secret.

agent.description: This agent's name in the engine config.

operatedBy.description: Who runs the engine's machine (engine.json operatedBy). PERSON (default, and when the shim cannot read the config): machine steps are the person's. AGENT: machine steps are the agent's (AGENT RUN_COMMAND); steps that need the admin stay the person's, on their own computer.

enforcement.description: ENGINE_AND_GUARD: the engine runs as its own OS user and the agent cannot read its credential, so every statement passes the engine's checks and the guard's. GUARD_ONLY: operatedBy is AGENT, or the engine runs in same-user mode, or the shim cannot read the config: the agent could connect with its credential directly, and the guard in Postgres still enforces intent, row limits, holds and signatures.

ready.description: True when no problem has severity ERROR: every tool is served.

reachable.description: False when the shim answers because the engine socket does not.

build.description: The engine's build version; the shim's when the engine is down.

state.description: OK: every migration of this build is installed. UPGRADE_AVAILABLE: only non-breaking migrations are missing; every tool is served. OUTDATED: a breaking migration is missing; every tool but status answers UNAVAILABLE reason GUARD_OUTDATED. NEWER: the guard is newer than this build (served). MISSING: no basalt_meta. UNKNOWN: the engine is down or the database cannot be reached.

build.description: The schema version this build installs.

setup.description: Setup from the person's laptop (basalt init --remote on the engine's machine, then basalt init --setup-code on the person's own computer).

state.description: PENDING: a setup code was made and its setup is not recorded yet. For an INSTALL code every tool but status answers UNAVAILABLE reason SETUP_PENDING (problem SETUP_NOT_RUN); for an AGENT or UPGRADE code the tools keep working with what is installed (problem SETUP_CHANGE_PENDING). EXPIRED: an INSTALL code past expiresAt (reason and problem SETUP_EXPIRED); a new code is needed. An expired AGENT or UPGRADE code is dropped, and the problem that called for it comes back. DONE: no setup pending, and setupId names the agent's latest recorded setup. NONE: no setup pending and none recorded (set up with basalt init and the admin connection string), or the engine is down and no setup is pending.

setupId.description: PENDING and EXPIRED: the pending code's. DONE: the latest recorded setup's.

expiresAt.description: PENDING and EXPIRED: when the code expires or expired.

fingerprint.description: PENDING: the pending code's setup fingerprint. Tell the person to check that basalt init --setup-code shows the same one.

served.description: Whether the engine serves the local approval and revert pages (short links).

url.description: The pages base URL links are built on.

vault.description: CONTRACT.md, Vault channel: the engine's connection to the hosted Vault and its identity. Absent when the engine is down.

state.description: OFF: engine.json vault is OFF, or pagesUrl is not the portal; short links use the local pages or long links. CONNECTING: dialling or authenticating. CONNECTED: authenticated (READY); portal short links work. UNREACHABLE: no READY for 30 seconds or more; the engine hands over long links and keeps retrying. KEY_ERROR: the key file is insecure, unreadable or invalid and was not replaced; long links until it is fixed or basalt engine rotate-key runs. Approvals work in every state.

engineId.description: The engine id (a fingerprint of its signing key), whenever the key file loads.

fingerprint.description: The engine id's first 16 characters in four groups, as the portal page shows it. The person compares the two.

registered.description: Whether at least one active passkey can approve held writes and sign reverts.

active.description: How many passkeys are active. Absent when the engine is down.

ledger.description: How much space the ledger takes and how long it is kept. Absent when the guard cannot be read.

bytes.description: The size of every table, index and TOAST table in basalt_meta, in bytes.

valuesKeptDays.description: Days a change's old and new values are kept before they are pruned (30).

recordsKeptDays.description: Days a ledger record is kept before it is deleted (365).

engineRecord.description: CONTRACT.md, Direct transport and Version 33: this engine's key as the agent's database records it. Absent when the engine is down.

state.description: RECORDED: the agent's database records this engine's key and has not revoked it. NOT_RECORDED: it does not record it (no setup code carried it, or the key was rotated since). REVOKED: the person revoked it; the engine hands over long links for this agent and refuses its portal sessions. UNKNOWN: the guard is older than version 33, the key file is refused, or the record could not be read.

url.description: The engine address recorded with the key, when there is one.

recordedAt.description: When the key was recorded (RECORDED, REVOKED).

update.description: status.update. Present only when a newer BasaltDB release is out (CONTRACT.md, Update notice). Tell the person; never upgrade without their OK.

latest.description: The newest release the person may be offered.

security.description: True when a release newer than the running build is a security release.

message.description: Starts WARNING: or SECURITY UPDATE:. Relay it to the person.

problems.description: Empty when everything is ready. Errors first.

code.description: PORTAL_MISMATCH (CONTRACT.md, CLI, basalt portal verify): the engine's daily check found the portal serving pages other than the ones this build embeds. DEV_LOCAL_PAGES (CONTRACT.md, Page origins): the engine.json devLocalPages development exception is on, so the pages are on the agent's machine. ENGINE_REVOKED (CONTRACT.md, Direct transport): the agent's database revoked this engine's key. DIRECT_NOT_SERVED (CONTRACT.md, Direct transport): the agent's database records an address for this engine, but directAddr is off, so a tunnel has nothing to forward to. LOCK_FILE_UNUSABLE (CONTRACT.md, On the engine, Lock files): the engine cannot open engine.json.lock or the agent's credential lock, so a finished setup is not written back. LEDGER_REINSTALLED (CONTRACT.md, Version 36): the ledger records that the guard was installed again and an engine set its pin of the old ledger aside; personMessage is the reinstall notice, to show the person as it is. PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE (CONTRACT.md, Plugins): an enabled plugin entry for this agent is not ready, so a wire.detect plugin fails the agent's requests to the AI provider closed until it is back or disabled. PLUGIN_NOT_TRUSTED (CONTRACT.md, Plugins): the engine refused to start a plugin entry for this agent because its signature, file hashes or file permissions failed (planned with service-mode isolation: or an agent's OS user is in the engine's group).

severity.description: ERROR: tools other than status do not work until it is fixed. WARNING: they work.

personMessage.description: The message the agent shows the person verbatim, keeping its line breaks; each URL on a line of its own (planned, M3.5) (CONTRACT.md, Showing links).

links.description: The URLs of personMessage with labels, in order; present exactly when personMessage holds a URL.
